h1: The Next Big Things in AWS for 2025
new.content: Skip to content Home > The Next Big Things in AWS for 2025 The Next Big Things in AWS for 2025 AWS in 2025 is transforming the cloud! Discover top trends and innovations driving the future of technology with 3RI Technologies Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri January 13, 2025 12:03 pm AWS will continue to grow and bring businesses solutions and new, unique, unmatched technologies as we approach 2025. Attending AWS Online Training can be a great beginning to becoming an AWS professional. In the dynamic world of technology, staying informed is key to staying relevant. As we look toward 2025, professionals and businesses are all asking the same question: what are the next big things in cloud computing? This guide explores the future of Amazon Web Services, uncovering the innovations in AI, data analytics, and serverless technology that will shape our digital world. Preparing for these advancements is not just smart, it’s essential for career growth. To build a strong foundation and be ready for tomorrow’s challenges, our comprehensive AWS Training in Pune provides the expert-led instruction needed to master the platform today and lead its evolution tomorrow. Key AWS Innovations and Trends to Watch Serverless Computing: A New Era Serverless computing is among AWS’s most exciting innovations: It indicates that server management is not a concern for AWS Developer Certification . While AWS handles everything behind the scenes, they can concentrate on creating code. Businesses can save time and money using AWS Lambda to run code only when necessary. We anticipate significantly more serverless services from AWS in 2025. Thanks to this, businesses can launch apps more quickly and save money on server maintenance. It is ideal for startups and small companies because of how easy it is to scale up or down with serverless computing. Characteristic Pros Example Serverless saves money and eliminates the need for server management AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate Traditional Servers Greater hardware control and increased administrative expenses EC2 instances Machine Learning and AI: Smarter Technology In the domains of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), AWS is already well-known. Companies can utilize AWS products like Amazon SageMaker to develop, train, and use machine learning models. Among the many applications of machine learning are business process automation and customer behavior prediction. We can anticipate that AWS will provide developers and companies with even more tools in the future to help them design more intelligent AI-powered solutions. Businesses can make better decisions and automate more processes with the aid of data-driven insights. An AWS Cloud Certification can assist you in acquiring the skills you need to go deeper into machine learning on AWS. Edge Computing and IoT: Real-Time Data Processing Edge computing has seen a meteoric rise in popularity due to the expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Instead of transmitting all of this data to a central cloud, edge computing enables data to be processed closer to the generation location, which is a vast improvement over traditional data transmission methods. The ability to access AWS services using edge devices is made possible, for instance, by AWS Greengrass. Many sectors rely on up-to-the-minute information, including healthcare and manufacturing. For instance, physicians can make quick choices by using real-time patient data. Edge computing makes this data without delays from the internet possible.| AWS training in Pune will be crucial for anyone in Mumbai or other major cities who wants to learn how to create and maintain these edge computing solutions. Sustainability: Green Cloud Computing In today’s world, leading a sustainable lifestyle is essential. This is a significant advancement in the battle against the negative environmental implications of cloud computing. But more effort needs to be made. In the coming years, AWS will probably provide more alternatives to assist companies in lowering their carbon footprint. AWS will make it easier to manage cloud resources’ performance and environmental impact, allowing businesses to monitor their energy consumption in the cloud and make more informed decisions about their IT infrastructure, such as running workloads in regions powered by renewable energy. Anyone interested in learning more about AWS’s sustainability initiatives may find everything they need to know by enrolling in an AWS Cloud Practitioner Certification. Security and Privacy: Keeping Data Safe Security in cloud computing will always be crucial, and AWS is consistently improving its security protocols. By 2025, AWS will continue to enhance its capabilities to protect confidential business data. Two products offered by AWS include AWS Shield, which protects against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), which controls who can access what resources. Why is AWS the world’s biggest cloud provider? 1. Timing Due to its early entry into the cloud industry, AWS was able to attract large, data-intensive clients like Netflix and AirBnB. Adoption is accompanied by inertia, as businesses were reluctant to consider switching to a competitor after deciding to use AWS. 2. Innovation However, being the first is insufficient. Throughout its leadership, AWS has prioritized innovation and advancement. All sizes of enterprises can now access the company’s early offerings, including Elastic Block Store (EBS), Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), and Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2).. To meet the needs of every industry and vertical, it is also constantly developing new services and enhancing existing ones. Many developers have grown to appreciate AWS since it has dominated the market for so long and are hesitant to switch to other cloud providers. AWS provides more stable and adaptable services in exchange for this commitment. Amazon’s Deep Lens, Sagemaker, and Sumerian are far ahead of the competition in terms of innovation. 3. Capacity Customers may access nearly infinite computation and storage capacity because of AWS’s significantly more vast infrastructure than other cloud providers. Large and expanding businesses must be able to depend on a cloud provider who can give what they require quickly. Therefore, this is an essential factor to consider—customers scale apps according to demand by utilizing AWS capabilities, Auto Scaling, and Elastic Load Balancing. AWS has a wealth of experience managing large corporations, as seen by its bank of well-known clients. 4. Regularity Customers of the cloud require stability. With its scalable, dependable, and secure global computing infrastructure, AWS provides all of that. It has broadened its geographic reach into significant areas to guarantee serviceability and uptime. If customers want rapid scaling, they are aware that computing instances may be swiftly spun up. Who Uses AWS? A 2022 Intricately analysis states that 1.45 million organizations are AWS customers. Its customers include companies of all sizes in different locations despite its tendency to focus on startups. This emphasis is consistent with the business’s public declarations regarding its plan to “get in early” with new businesses to increase their use as the startups’ requirements develop. These endeavors yield results: With an annual growth rate of 42.2%, startups and SMBs are the AWS customer base sector with the quickest growth rate. With almost 123,000 clients, the Internet sector accounts for the most significant share of clients. With 48,807 clients, the media sector is the next largest industry segment. AWS Customers List Name Industry Region Salesforce Healthcare United States Netflix Media & Entertainment United States Coca-Cola Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) Americas Toyota Automotive United States Zomato Hospitality India Wealthfront Financial Services United States ŠKODA Automotive Czech Republic Panasonic Manufacturing United States Johnson & Johnson Life Sciences United States Airbnb Travel United States How do companies use AWS? AWS’s application portfolio is nearly as extensive as the cloud itself. However, companies who successfully use AWS typically see a sharp increase in speed and efficiency and a decrease in deployment time. Here are a few instances: Water utility firms can better evaluate the health of water management systems and water/wastewater treatment facilities by using AWS to produce three cloud-native software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions from Innovyze, a software startup Autodesk bought in March 2021. By moving data from on-premises to a SaaS solution, scalability was significantly increased, and deployment and time to market were shortened. The sports gaming startup FanDuel Group (FanDuel) moved four linear live-stream channels to Amazon Web Services (AWS) between December 2021 and January 2022. Their third-party video-streaming provider couldn’t manage all the live broadcasts available all day and night, allowing customers to gamble almost in real time. To scale without sacrificing the viewing experience, FanDuel turned to AWS Cloudfront. Cloudfront is a content delivery network solution designed to provide developers with exceptional performance, scalability, security, and ease of use. Toyota leverages AWS to fuel innovation throughout all of its businesses. A next-generation data lake constructed on AWS utilizing Amazon S3, AWS Glue, and Amazon Redshift is used by Toyota North America to collect and analyze data from many production sites. This cloud-based analytics system can track the manufacturing history of each car, enhance customer service, and make smarter decisions regarding the supply chain. The transportation company Scania discovered that its on-premises servers were not able to manage the increasing volume of its connected-truck services, which are Internet of Things (IoT) products that collect vehicle data in almost real-time and transmit updated instructions and data back to vehicles, as its clientele and services expanded. Scania can scale as needed with lower latency and better security by utilizing solutions like AWS Lambda. The company has also created a new hybrid design using AWS services to retain network links with telecom carriers. When Zalando, an online fashion and lifestyle company, moved its media management system to Amazon CloudFront, it improved developer control and consumer experience. To ensure sustained growth and a unique customer experience, the company needed developer insight and power, which CloudFront provided by improving the media management and delivery systems that impact the consumer experience. With the petabyte-level data lake it oversees, Salesforce’s Unified Intelligence Platform (UIP) Team set out to improve data processing and analysis efficiently and cost-effectively. Several instance-provisioning methods created a scalable, elastic computing architecture from Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2). Salesforce saves more than $1 million a month because of this improved computing infrastructure, which can process as much data in less time. Key Takeaway s Market Domination and Ongoing Innovation: AWS continues to lead the cloud industry because of its unparalleled capacity and steady innovation. Strategic Alliances for Improved Experience: To optimize data and provide better developer and customer experiences, AWS collaborates with industry leaders such as Salesforce and Zalando. Simplified Cloud Management with Partners: Businesses like Spacelift work with AWS to streamline cloud operations, which improves user management effectiveness. 3RI’s Contribution to AWS Evolution: 3RI AWS continues to empower firms like 3RI to develop scalable solutions, supporting the competitive advantages and the next generation of cloud solutions. h1: The Symbiotic Relationship: Understanding the Role of Microservices in DevOps
new.content: Skip to content Home > The Symbiotic Relationship: Understanding the Role of Microservices in DevOps The Symbiotic Relationship: Understanding the Role of Microservices in DevOps Microservices play a crucial role in DevOps by enabling agility, scalability, and resilience in application deployment. Their modular structure allows DevOps teams to streamline development, automate testing, and manage independent services efficiently, boosting productivity and reducing downtime. Discover the benefits of combining microservices with DevOps for optimal flexibility. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri October 10, 2024 7:03 pm In the quest for faster development cycles and more resilient applications, the synergy between microservices in DevOps has become a cornerstone of modern software engineering. Understanding what are microservices in DevOps reveals how this architectural style, which structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services, aligns perfectly with the collaborative and agile principles of DevOps. Effectively implementing DevOps for microservices allows teams to independently develop, deploy, and scale services, drastically improving efficiency and innovation speed. For those in Pune looking to master these transformative practices, our comprehensive DevOps course in Pune provides the in-depth knowledge and hands-on skills required. This article will explore the pivotal role microservices play in a successful DevOps culture. Technology is developing faster than ever. People use the Internet extensively for daily tasks, including shopping, banking, and medical care. Due to this, service providers must meet this constantly rising customer demand, which, in addition to: Changing needs of the user The ever-difficult security environment This compels service providers to switch from traditional software development methodologies to Agile and DevOps techniques , enabling them to adjust to evolving demands promptly. Another trend is microservices-based architectures, which build applications as multiple loosely connected services. This article’s subject is the role of microservices within the DevOps methodology. How Microservices Architecture Enables Key DevOps Principles Modern application developers typically welcome the changes brought about by a microservices-based architecture. When businesses embrace change, they find that productivity is rising at an astounding rate and that customers who need flexible, scalable apps can get their requests fulfilled much faster. Microservices have several important advantages for DevOps workers, including: Deployability: Microservices’ enhanced agility facilitates the deployment of new service versions, enhancing its deployability—shorter cycles for development, testing, and deployment cause this agility. Additionally, microservices can offer the adaptability required to use security, replication, persistence, and monitoring configurations unique to each service. Reliability: Failure of a microservice affects only that microservice and its users. If a monolithic application has a bug, the monolith might not work. Availability: In a monolithic application, updating a service version usually requires restarting the monolith; however, updating a particular microservice only causes minor downtime. Scalability: Pools, clusters, and grids are tools microservices can use to grow independently. Microservices’ deployment feature makes them perfect for the cloud’s elasticity. Modifiability: The flexibility to include new frameworks, libraries, data sources, and more is a crucial feature of microservices. Microservices, which are modular components with loose coupling, are easier to work with and enable dynamic discovery and binding through a registry. Management: Microservices can benefit from the agile technique, which divides the task of developing an application into smaller, more autonomous teams. Because microservices use a standard toolbox for operations and development, they boost DevOps productivity. This common toolkit creates processes for needs, dependencies, issues, and common language. It consequently facilitates communication between Devs and Ops, enabling those parties to collaborate on an issue and effectively resolve a build configuration or script. Microservices and DevOps perform best when used in combination. DevOps Basics The method companies use to develop, deploy, and maintain software has changed dramatically with the advent of DevOps. DevOps transforms the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC) into a more cooperative procedure. A DevOps team comprises cross-disciplinary team members who contribute their unique skills to the DevOps process; unlike the traditional SDLC, the Dev, QA, and Ops teams are viewed as distinct autonomous entities. As a result, the DevOps team is far more adaptable and can better communicate with bigger teams like QA and Dev. In the end, this results in a development environment that is quicker, more agile, more effective, and has predictable update cycles and deployments. Furthermore, DevOps makes it possible to develop SaaS business models, allowing companies to generate ongoing income while providing a stable, updated service that constantly improves. An organization can get numerous advantages from implementing DevOps. But to reap those rewards, you must apply DevOps correctly using standardized ideas and appropriate DevOps tools like: Automated examination Ongoing incorporation Platforms for continuous delivery Combining Software Development with DevOps The fundamental elements of management and development will not change. However, the technological stack you employ in a given application will vary based on your: The audience Platform requirements from both the internal and the external Here, we’ll review the essential topics to consider when building a DevOps pipeline. Are you looking after Career Guidance from Experts? Book Now Want Free Career Counseling? Just fill in your details, and one of our expert will call you ! Email Phone Send Version Control Version control is the foundation of any process in DevOps. Code repositories like Bitbucket, Azure Repos, GitLab, and technologies like Git make source code management more accessible than ever. With version control over the application, these solutions let developers work together without interfering with one other’s work. The DevOps process now includes version-controlled repositories for managing database code as well. One way to summarize version controlling is as follows: Lowers the number of code conflicts Improves development’s efficiency and visibility Makes it simple to revert to earlier versions in case of Automation Since DevOps depends on automated chores for speedier development, automation is the second important factor to consider. Automating repetitive manual processes is necessary for the DevOps team, and they should always search for new tasks to automate. For example, automated technologies like Cucumber, Selenium, and Appium can significantly assist the application testing phase because they allow users to automate most test cases. Moreover, automation Lowers the likelihood of human mistake Cuts down on time spent on tedious work Allows team members to concentrate on more crucial issues Deployment Strategy The deployment strategy is the next thing to think about. With the increasing popularity of cloud-based apps and all the benefits of cloud-based deployments, most DevOps deployment stages aim to create highly available and scalable cloud infrastructure. One of the things driving this move to cloud-based deployments is containerized apps. With the help of containers, users may build portable, separated application environments with all the dependencies needed to deploy anywhere. Platforms such as Rancher and Kubernetes offer robust orchestration features for containerized deployments. Automating software deployments and packaging is also quite crucial in this case. Organizations can build a pipeline covering every SDLC stage with a version-controlled, automated DevOps pipeline and an appropriate deployment strategy. Now that we know the main elements of a DevOps pipeline let’s examine how microservices impact each aspect. Want to learn all about DevOps – Check Out Now! Microservices Overview A distinct approach to development from traditional monolithic programs is microservices architecture (where the entire application is reviewed and developed as a single entity). Different loosely coupled services make up the application thanks to the microservice architecture. As an illustration, let’s look at an online marketplace: The entire platform, including payment processing, shopping cart functionality, and inventory management, is designed as one unit in the conventional development process. Development and deployment co-occur for every modification. However, the application will be divided into separate services (payment, shopping cart, and inventory management services) using the microservices design, allowing them to be created and implemented separately. This method lessens their influence on the application by isolating any problems with that particular service. Microservices-based applications benefit significantly from the DevOps method since it makes development simple, offers smooth updates, and handles individual services without running the risk of the entire program failing. Role of Microservices in DevOps Let’s look at a DevOps pipeline to create a microservices-based application and better understand the function of microservices in DevOps. Microservices initially alter the way companies approach development. Since everything has been divided into discrete services, development teams may be split to concentrate on each service. The development will, therefore, have a more manageable scope and adaptable development methodology. Overall flexibility This adaptability enables DevOps teams to handle problems efficiently. For example, the development team can address a production bug and deploy the fixed service with minimal downtime and no impact on other services’ SDLC. Additionally, developers can create and implement any new features that a service needs without impeding the work of those developing other services. The decoupled design streamlines the development and testing process and allows for independent service modification. Containers Containerization is another component that improves and adds to microservices-based systems. While optimizing the continuous delivery process, packaging each service as a container image minimizes complexity. With all dependencies and requirements contained within the container, services can function as independent entities. As a result, the services can communicate with any other system and become reusable and system-agnostic. Take Action! Book a Free Expert Session Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send APIs APIs are an additional component that enhances microservices. Users utilizing decoupled services want a reliable means of communication to exchange information amongst services. With the help of APIs, developers can securely harden their services, provide an interface compatible with all platforms, and only expose the pertinent endpoints and data. This becomes an issue when developing system-agnostic reusable services. Automation Automation comes next. A microservices architecture allows for the automating of most tasks related to testing, packaging, and deployment for individual services. Every service has its own DevOps pipeline, so problems with one automated operation don’t impact the others. Additionally, feedback loops get significantly shorter when using the streamlined codebase to address defects. Microservices work best with automation during the deployment and maintenance phases. Upon completion of testing and uploading the container image to a container registry, the deployment procedure will initiate an automated operation to launch the service as a container. Streamlining the deployment process involves removing the need for specific network setups or prioritizing dependency management. Enhanced Accessibility and Flexibility Finally, service containers placed in clusters and managed by an orchestration platform automatically improve the application’s availability and scalability. It is possible to promptly swap out a malfunctioning service container for a new one. It is possible to build a new container to handle a spike in demand if a service is experiencing a high load. This makes it possible to implement scale-out techniques without depending on prohibitively expensive scale-up strategies based on resource increases. Claim your free expert counseling session today! h1: Time Series Forecasting and Perform Advanced Analytics in Power BI
new.content: Skip to content Home > Time Series Forecasting and Perform Advanced Analytics in Power BI Time Series Forecasting and Perform Advanced Analytics in Power BI In this blog article, we will learn how to get the forecasting results in Power BI by using Times series and What if Parameters forecasting graphs. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri June 14, 2024 6:02 pm Time Series Forecasting and Advanced Analytics in Power BI One of the main components of machine learning is time series forecasting , which enables you to plan and modify your marketing initiatives to meet your objectives. Time series forecasting in Power BI enables organizations to predict trends and make data-driven decisions with precision. With advanced capabilities like Power BI forecasting and BI advanced analytics, professionals can uncover deep business insights from past data patterns. Whether you’re analyzing future sales, market behavior, or operations, mastering Power BI time series analytics is a game-changer. 3RI Technologies offers expert-led Power BI Online Training to help you become proficient in these powerful tools. If you’re ready to upgrade your skills and lead in data analytics, now is the time to start. In this blog article, we will learn how to get the forecasting results in Power BI by using Times series and What if Parameters forecasting graphs. Unlock Predictive Insights with Power BI Forecasting Techniques The phrase “times series forecasting” refers to the process of developing an AI prediction based on historical data and scientific techniques. It involves building data models via historical analysis and using them to draw attention to patterns and enhance your decision-making in the future. It is the technique of utilizing statistics to foresee outcomes by studying data across time. However, when dealing with variable fluctuations, accuracy is not absolute. Keep reading to learn more about how Times Series predictions might help you make better decisions. Explore your Power BI Skills with Power BI Online Course Getting your Data into Power BI Since BI decommissioned its Facebook ads connector, we will use an alternative connector to connect Meta Ads to Power BI. Method 1: Times Series forecasting Using the Analysis Pane in Microsoft Power BI For the time series analysis to function correctly, you must first import your data into Power BI. Verify that your data has dated. You also require a minimum of 90 days of data. 1. As seen in the illustration below, choose the Line chart Visual. 2. Assign the X and Y axes to the Date and clicks fields. 3. Select the analytics panel and activate the forecast feature. You can modify the prediction length and the confidence interval in the figure above based on your analysis needs. Method 2: Using What if Parameters to visualize variables BIs with Power How about using parameters, like cost, impressions, clicks, conversions, and so forth, to forecast numbers based on particular conditions? Consider increasing campaign ad expenditure to see how it will affect conversion rates. Another strategy is developing a marketing mix highlighting how investing in various channels would impact earnings. Are you looking after Career Guidance from Experts? Book Now Want Free Career Counseling? Just fill in your details, and one of our expert will call you ! Email Phone Send Performing Analytics in Power BI : What Is It? Using this potent business intelligence tool, Power BI analytics entails turning unstructured data into insightful understandings. With interactive dashboards and reports, Power BI users may connect to various data sources, including databases, spreadsheets, and cloud services, and then clean, model, and visualize the data. Using the platform’s advanced analytics tools, which include AI and machine learning integrations, customers can identify trends, project results, and make data-driven choices. Users may develop a data-driven culture inside their organization using Power BI to build custom graphics, conduct ad hoc research, and share insights with others. Its powerful features ensure that stakeholders always have access to the most recent information: real-time data monitoring, natural language queries, and automated data refreshes. Doing analytics in Power BI simplifies the data for the analysis process and makes it understandable to both technical and non-technical people. Learn the Power BI skills online from Industry Expert Trainers only at Power BI Course in Pune Using What-If Parameters in Power BI Visuals With Power BI’s what-if parameter capability, you can design unique “what-if” scenarios that are perfect for predicting. For instance, a business might see a consistent annual revenue increase of 10%. But what would happen if they wanted to project various growth rates for the upcoming months or year and see how that would impact the KPIs in their Power BI report? Using what-if parameters, they can accomplish this quickly and simply. This tutorial will add a what-if option to our opportunity value estimate to dynamically change the growth rate. We’ll display the impact as a line graph with three months’ projected opportunity values plotted against actual values. Choose the Modeling tab from the ribbon, then click “New Parameter” to create a what-if parameter. This will open a dialog box where we can enter the parameter name (Opportunity Growth Rate), the data type (decimal), and the desired values (from -1 to 1 in increments of 0.01) for the parameter. If the user does not pick a value for the option, it will take the default value of 0. Enter 0 for this parameter. The choice to add a slicer to the page should then be carefully considered, as we will require it to be able to modify our projected growth rate dynamically. Essentially, this what-if option will produce a table where each of the various values entered into the range will have its own column. It will also make a measure that returns the chosen value from that table. To determine the anticipated potential value, we will use this metric. Make a date table using the present date range in the data and the dates for as many months into the future as necessary to observe how this forecast performs for upcoming months. In this example, the anticipated time frame we will utilize is three months. We must establish a measure using the following DAX formula to compute the anticipated sales: Opportunity Forecast = IF( MAX ( ‘Opportunity Calendar'[Date] ) > DATE(2021, 09, 21), CALCULATE ( SUM ( Opportunities[Value] ), DATEADD ( ‘Opportunity Calendar'[Date], -1, YEAR ) ) * ( 1+’Opportunity Growth Rate'[Opportunity Growth Rate Value] ), SUM ( Opportunities[Value] ) ) If the dates fall above the latest date in our dataset (21 Sep 2021), this DAX formula will provide the anticipated opportunity value (raised by the opportunity growth rate from our what-if parameter); if not, it will return the actual opportunity value. If you were using this DAX formula on current data, you would need to substitute the function TODAY() for the part containing DATE(2021, 09, 21). Finally, we can create a line chart with the actual opportunity value and this opportunity projection measure so that the two lines overlap. new.content: Skip to content Home > 5 Expert Tips to Crack Your Data Visualization Interview 5 Expert Tips to Crack Your Data Visualization Interview Professionals with experience in Data Visualization are in high demand due to the rapid advancements in the field of Data Analytics. Today, we'll talk about 5 tips to crack the interview to help you land your next Data Visualization job. Table of Contents madan November 27, 2023 5:50 pm Professionals with experience in Data Visualization are in high demand due to the rapid advancements in the field of Data Analytics. A Data Visualization specialist’s role is becoming increasingly important as companies attempt to leverage their data to make informed decisions. Work in this highly competitive industry requires technological proficiency and a thorough understanding of the art and science of transforming complex data into insightful graphics. Today, we’ll talk about 5 tips to crack the interview to help you land your next Data Visualization job. Why Data Visualization Skills Matter in Today’s Job Market As data becomes central to business decision-making, professionals who can translate numbers into compelling visuals have a clear advantage. Employers are actively looking for candidates with hands-on experience in data visualization techniques and familiarity with widely used data visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI. Whether you’ve taken a certified data visualization course or worked on self-initiated projects, showcasing your ability to communicate insights visually is now a key interview differentiator. Recruiters especially value candidates who demonstrate practical application, not just theory. For learners in tech-driven cities like Pune, the rise of job-linked Data analytics courses in Pune and online data visualization programs has made skill-building more accessible. These programs often align with placement opportunities and are tailored to current industry needs. If you’re preparing for a data-related role—whether in analytics, business intelligence, or data science—sharpening your visual storytelling skills is a smart step toward interview success. Upskill with a Structured Data Visualization Course 1. Portfolio Showcase Your portfolio is the blank page that shows how much you’ve learned about how to present facts. There’s more to the report than just graphs and charts. It shows how you’ve grown, how creative you are, and how well you can turn data into useful information. You should have a lot of different projects in your portfolio to show that you can work with varying types of data and companies. Ensure that each piece in your portfolio has an interesting story, such as the problem you solved, the data issues you ran into, or the impact of your visualizations. Your professional skills, as well as your imagination and ability to come up with new ideas, should all be shown off in a well-organized portfolio. Employers want more than just standard answers; they want to see how you can show data in a way that no one else can. Read your resume and consider how it shows your skills have changed. Focus on the lessons you’ve learned and how you’ve grown as a Data Visualization worker. Learn the Power BI skills from Industry Expert Trainers only at Power BI Course in Pune 2. Mastery of Visualization Tools Working with Data Visualization requires proficiency with the necessary tools. Whether it’s because of these programs’ intuitive user interfaces (like Tableau and Power BI) or the versatility offered by Python modules (like Matplotlib and Seaborn), mastery of these tools is crucial. To demonstrate your expertise with these technologies during the interview, evaluate specific projects in which you have produced impactful visualizations using them. Explain how you chose the right tool for a specific task. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each tool and how your choice will impact the visualization’s overall power. Show off your adaptability by showcasing your skill with various tools and emphasizing your commitment to staying current with the latest advancements in data visualization technologies. This demonstrates your technical proficiency and reassures the interviewer about your ability to work well with their present workflow. 3. Storytelling with Data Telling a relatable story is just as important as displaying numbers when using Data Visualization. Discuss how you structure your visuals to communicate an engaging and logical tale throughout the interview. This will enable you to demonstrate your storytelling prowess. Provide instances of your work on projects where you used data storytelling to influence decisions and make things easier for people to grasp. Knowing your audience and tailoring your story to their level of understanding is essential for crafting an effective data story. Engagingly communicating complex concepts is crucial, regardless of the audience you are speaking to – C-suite executives or colleagues in other departments. Discuss the process of developing a storyline, the usage of annotations, and the systematic placement of essential concepts in your visualizations. This will demonstrate your ability to communicate effectively and commitment to ensuring that your illustrations result in meaningful action. Are you looking after Career Guidance from Experts? Book Now Want Free Career Counseling? Just fill in your details, and one of our expert will call you ! Email Phone Send 4. Attention to Aesthetics and Clarity Aesthetics and clarity go hand in hand in the field of Data Visualization. Your images should be informative and visually engaging. Throughout the interview, examine your approach to color theory, font choices, and overall design concepts. During the interview, you should discuss color theory, font choice, and design in general. Discuss how you achieve a balance between originality and simplicity to ensure that your visualizations are not just appealing but also understandable. Professionals who can make images that are both correct and appealing to the eye are in high demand. Paying attention to how your visualizations look should make them more powerful overall, making them easier to remember and more attractive to your audience. Showcases from your portfolio where your design choices were essential in getting your message across, and discuss any problems you ran into when balancing good looks with the need for clear communication. Excel in the art of Data Analytics by enrolling in our Data Analytics Course in Pune. 5. Problem-Solving Demonstrations Finally, data representation is a way to solve problems in the real world. An essential part of your interview is showing how your images solved complex problems. You should be ready to show the interviewer specific examples of how your visualizations helped you make better decisions or gain useful insights. Talk about how you solved problems from the start of a project, including finding the biggest problems, cleaning and changing the data, and choosing the best ways to display it. Show how your ideas worked by showing real-world outcomes or results that came from your visualizations. Employers are interested in more than how technically skilled you are; they want to know how you can use your skills to make a real difference in their business. The Closing Note Succeeding in a Data Visualization interview demands a comprehensive strategy beyond technical expertise. These are the best tips to crack interview for the same. Therefore, you position yourself as a well-rounded data visualization professional by showcasing a carefully chosen portfolio that tells your story, proving your proficiency with visualization tools, stressing your data storytelling abilities, paying attention to clarity and aesthetics, and showcasing your problem-solving skills. Remember that it’s not enough to make graphics; you also need to write a story that turns data into ideas that can be used. new.content: Skip to content Home > Top 10 ETL Testing Interview Questions And Answers Top 10 ETL Testing Interview Questions And Answers When you are going to attend the ETL interview, you get puzzled about how to answers the questions that will ask by the interviewer. To make this task easier and flawless, the article has assembled a list of questions where you will find the top 10 ELT testing interview questions and Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri October 17, 2019 5:04 pm Top 10 ETL testing interview questions and answers When you are going to attend the ETL interview, you get puzzled about how to answers the questions that will ask by the interviewer. To make this task easier and flawless, the article has assembled a list of questions where you will find the top 10 ELT testing interview questions and answers, which will give you a quick way to read and learn these. These have been designed in a very precise and influencing way; thereby, the interviewee will able to answer confidently, quickly, and impressively. Since there are many questions related to the ETL interview, the following assembled is the best and perfect to go through as these have been asked as of now. Concisely, you must give top priority to these and read them comprehensively. Q1. What is ETL and explain why ETL testing is required? Answer: The term ETL stands for Extract, Transform, and Load. This software is used for data need to analyze and forecast the future of any business. ETL comprises three-term; all have different meanings and functions. The term is extracting means seeking the data and elimination of all the data from the source file. The term transforming means the process of transferring the data to any specific file along with loading that data to the target system accordingly requested. The term loads mean to verify that data is loaded at the stipulated time to enhance performance and scalability. Q2. What do you mean by the surrogate key? Answer: The role of the surrogate key is to model any object or entity. It is regarded as the unique key intended to know about the primary identifier of any entity or object that is not derived from other databases. Besides, a surrogate key is not always determined as a primary key, and its’ all relied on the database. It’s depending upon the situation of the database if it is a current kind, then storage will be given to the current database, and it always has one relationship between the primary and surrogate keys while if it is temporal kind, then there will be many to one relationship between the surrogate key and primary. Email Phone Send Q3: What is partitioning, hash partitioning, and round-robin partitioning? With an intention is to improve performance, transactions get subdivided, which is called partitioning. It allows the Informatica server to establish a multitude of links to different sources. There are two types of partitioning: Hash partitioning Round-robin partitioning Hash partitioning is used to partition keys in favour of group data in the middle of the partitions Informatica server when the hash function is applied. Briefly, it is used to enables the groups of rows with a similar partitioning key in the similar partition required to be secured. Round-Robin partitioning is used to divide the Informatica data evenly to all partitions. It is used only where the number of rows is similar to the process. Answer: In a multi-dimensional model, a fact determined at the central part, having all the measures required to be analyzed. There are three types of facts: Additive: In additive fact, a measure is used to analyze arithmetic calculations by permitting all or a few dimensions. Semi-additive: In semi-additive facts, a measure is used to analyze arithmetic calculations by permitting a few dimensions only. Non-additive: In non-additive facts, a measure is never involved in arithmetic functions with the help of dimension. Q5. What is the difference between ETL testing and database testing? Answer: Database testing is used to focus on the integration of data, while ETL testing basically involves focusing on business intelligence reporting. The tools used for database testing are QTP and selenium while QuerySurge, Informatica, Cognos, are tools used in ETL testing. Database testing is used normalized data, while ETL testing usually has deformalized data. During the analysis of data, database testing always has architectural implementation impacts, while ETL testing results in a potential impact on data. Q6. Do you about the staging area? Answer: The term data sagging is used when there is a need to assemble the processes required to prepare the source system data, which is further loaded or transferred into the data warehouse. Q7. What is a slow-changing dimension? Answer: This question is often asked during the interview process, and only a few know about it. The purpose of a slowly changing dimension means it tends to change very slowly or steadily. It means the data available in this process will alter or amend very slowly as compared to others. Q8: What are the types of data warehouse applications and also explain the difference between data mining and data warehousing? Answer: There are three types of data warehouse applications have, such as: Data Mining Info Processing Analytical Processing The primary difference between data mining and data warehousing is in the case of data mining; there is a process of fetching hidden predictive information from the massive databases while data warehousing is used for analytical processing of the data in a steady way. Moreover, data warehousing is used to collect data from a multitude of sources into a single repository. Wishing to start a career as a Software Tester? h1: 10 Fascinating Python Applications in the Real World
new.content: Skip to content Home > 10 Fascinating Python Applications in the Real World 10 Fascinating Python Applications in the Real World From AI to finance, Python powers many industries. Here are 10 real-world applications every student should know to stay ahead in tech fields Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri October 25, 2024 5:36 pm Python’s popularity is well-founded, as it has become one of the most widely used programming languages in recent years. It is the perfect option for developers of all skill levels because of its straightforward syntax, readability, and adaptability. Python is useful for generating artificial intelligence, analyzing data, and creating online applications. In this blog post, we’ll explore Python’s top ten fascinating applications in real-world scenarios, illustrating its impact across various industries. If you are considering enrolling in a Python course in Pune or are simply curious about what Python can do, this exploration will provide valuable insights. Have you ever wondered about the real-world impact of the code you learn? The real world applications of python are more extensive and impressive than you might imagine, making it one of today’s most popular programming languages. This guide explores the most impactful python applications in real world scenarios, showcasing how it powers everything from streaming services to artificial intelligence. We will provide concrete examples of python applications and delve into python real world applications in data analysis, machine learning, and web development. These real life applications of python and real world python applications demonstrate its power and flexibility. If and want to build your own innovative solutions, our industry-leading Python Training in Pune will equip you with the skills you need to succeed. Real-World Python Applications You Interact with Daily The benefits of using Python for application development must be understood before we can discuss particular applications.Here are some key benefits: Ease of Learning: Beginners find Python easy to learn because of its straightforward and intuitive syntax. This allows new programmers to focus on grasping programming concepts rather than getting bogged down by complex grammar rules. Versatility: Python works with several programming paradigms, including procedural, object-oriented, and functional. Developers are able to choose the style that best suits their project’s requirements due to its versatility. Rich Ecosystem: Python has many frameworks and tools, such as Pandas for analyzing data and Django for creating web applications. These tools enhance productivity and accelerate development processes. Community Support: There is a large and vibrant Python community that provides a multitude of resources, including forums, tutorials, and comprehensive documentation. For ongoing learning and troubleshooting, this support system is vital. Cross-Platform Compatibility: Python applications are accessible and widely usable because they can operate without modifications on a number of operating systems, such as Linux, macOS, and Windows. Rapid Development: Python is perfect for prototyping and iterative development because of its ease of use and abundance of libraries, which enable quicker development cycles. Integration Capabilities: Python’s ease of integration with other languages and technologies promotes teamwork and lets developers take advantage of pre-existing applications and systems. These benefits make Python an excellent choice for various applications across different industries, fostering innovation and efficiency. Top 10 Python Applications in the Real World 1. Web Development Frameworks such as Django and Flask have made Python popular for building websites. Django, in particular, is known for its “batteries-included” philosophy, which provides many built-in features, such as authentication, URL routing, and an ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) system. Django is used for the back-end architecture of several well-known websites, such as Instagram and Pinterest, demonstrating Python’s capacity to manage applications with significant traffic. In contrast, Flask is a micro-framework that provides simplicity and flexibility for smaller applications. Its lightweight nature makes it suitable for projects that require a straightforward implementation without the overhead of a full-fledged framework. With Flask, developers can quickly prototype applications and build RESTful APIs, allowing for rapid development and deployment. 2. Data Science and Analytics Data scientists can produce high-quality graphs and charts to represent their findings visually, making complex data more digestible. These tools empower data scientists to analyze complex datasets, derive insights, and communicate their findings effectively, making Python indispensable in industries such as finance, healthcare, and marketing. 3. Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Python is at the leading edge of data science, which has become one of the most important areas in the IT sector. Python is the best option for the visualization and analysis of data, mainly because of modules like Matplotlib, NumPy, and Pandas. Pandas facilitate data analysis and manipulation, which makes working with structured data easier. Data Frames and other data structures offered by this library make it easier to clean, transform, and analyze data. NumPy supports large, multi-dimensional arrays and matrices and offers a variety of mathematical functions for working with these arrays. Matplotlib enables Python users to produce both simple and dynamic visual representations. Furthermore, Python is crucial for the progress of two of the most important technologies of our time: machine learning and artificial intelligence. Developers tend to focus on creating algorithms instead of becoming mired down by complicated syntax due to the language’s readability and simplicity. Email Phone Send Libraries like TensorFlow, Keras, and Scikit-learn provide robust frameworks for building machine-learning models. TensorFlow is an open-source numerical computation toolkit that facilitates and speeds up machine learning, especially for deep learning applications. With its user-friendly interface for model design and training, Keras, which is based on TensorFlow, streamlines the process of creating neural networks. Scikit-learn offers straightforward and efficient data mining and analysis tools, including clustering, regression, and classification techniques. These libraries have led to advancements in various applications, from image recognition and natural language processing to autonomous vehicles, showcasing Python’s capabilities in the realm of AI. Organizations like Google, Spotify, and Netflix use Python to enhance customer experience by using predictive analytics and personalized recommendations. 4. Automation and Scripting Python is a powerful tool for automation, allowing programmers to create scripts that carry out repetitive operations automatically. System administrators and DevOps specialists who must effectively manage servers and workflows would especially benefit from this feature. Data entry, file management, and report creation can all be made more efficient by automating these tasks with Python.For instance, Python scripts can automate the extraction of data from spreadsheets, perform calculations, and generate comprehensive reports, saving hours of manual labor. Libraries like Selenium are used for web automation, allowing users to interact with web applications programmatically. By automating these processes, organizations may reduce the likelihood of human error and save time, which will ultimately increase productivity and efficiency across a variety of operations. Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session? Book Now Get FREE career counselling from Experts ! Email Phone Send 5. Game Development Python is a useful tool in the game development industry, even though it might not be the first language that comes to mind. Libraries like Pygame provide the necessary functionality to create 2D games quickly and easily. Pygame offers modules for sound, graphics, and game physics, allowing developers to focus on creating engaging gameplay rather than dealing with complex engine architecture. This makes Python particularly suitable for prototyping game ideas or creating educational games, making it a popular choice among beginner developers. Several indie game developers and hobbyists have utilized Python to create entertaining games that can be easily shared and played across various platforms. Additionally, Python’s integration with game engines like Unity through plugins allows for more complex game development processes. 6. Internet of Things (IoT) Python is a key component of the Internet of Things (IoT), which is revolutionizing the way we interact with commonplace objects. Python’s adaptability is essential for IoT development as smart homes and connected gadgets become more common. Libraries like Micro Python and Circuit Python enable Python to run on microcontrollers, making it possible to develop IoT applications that can be deployed on small devices. For example, developers can create smart home devices that respond to user commands, collect environmental data, or control lighting and heating systems. Python’s ease of use allows developers to create connected systems that communicate with each other, collect data, and respond to user inputs in real-time. Additionally, the ability to use Python in conjunction with platforms like Raspberry Pi further enhances its applicability in the IoT space, enabling the creation of innovative and interactive devices. 7. Cybersecurity Python has gained popularity in cybersecurity due to its ability to create tools for penetration testing, malware analysis, and automation of security tasks. Python is used by security experts to create scripts that run different security assessments, examine network traffic, and look for vulnerabilities. Libraries such as Scapy facilitate packet manipulation and network analysis, while tools like Nmap allow for network discovery and security auditing. Python’s extensive libraries, like requests and Beautiful Soup, can be used to scrape and analyze web data for potential vulnerabilities. With Python, cybersecurity experts can develop tools to identify security weaknesses, automate the testing of software, and create scripts to enhance network security measures. Its ability to handle complex tasks with minimal code makes it an essential language in the cybersecurity toolkit, enabling professionals to develop robust security solutions. 8. Scientific Computing In academia and scientific research, Python has become the language of choice for scientific computing. Libraries like SciPy and SymPy offer strong capabilities for symbolic mathematics and numerical computations. SciPy is perfect for scientific research since it expands on NumPy and provides more features for interpolation, integration, and optimization. SymPy, on the other hand, is a library for symbolic mathematics, allowing researchers to perform algebraic operations in Python. These capabilities enable scientists and researchers to conduct simulations, analyze experimental data, and solve complex mathematical problems, reinforcing Python’s importance in the scientific community. Institutions like NASA and CERN have adopted Python to assist in data analysis and simulation tasks, showcasing its relevance in cutting-edge research. 9. Web Scraping Web scraping is a technique used to extract data from websites, and Python’s libraries make this process efficient and straightforward. Two well-known libraries that make web scraping easier are Beautiful Soup and Scrapy, which let programmers quickly parse HTML and XML data. Web scraping is widely used for data gathering, market analysis, and competitive research. For example, companies might acquire insights that guide their plans by using web scraping to collect consumer reviews from many platforms or track competitors’ costs. Additionally, researchers can scrape data for academic studies or data analysis projects, allowing for comprehensive data collection in various fields. Python’s capabilities in web scraping also extend to automation, enabling developers to create scripts that automatically gather and process data on a scheduled basis, enhancing efficiency and accuracy in data-driven tasks. 10. Blockchain Development As blockchain technology continues to evolve, Python is becoming increasingly important in this space. Python’s readability and flexibility make it an excellent choice for developing decentralized apps (dApps) and smart contracts. Frameworks like Django can be used to build the back-end of blockchain applications, while libraries like web3.py enable interaction with the Ethereum blockchain. Python’s ease of use allows developers to focus on creating innovative solutions that harness the power of blockchain technology, making it an attractive choice for startups and established companies alike. Moreover, Python’s ability to handle complex data structures and perform cryptographic operations positions it well for various blockchain-related applications, including cryptocurrency wallets and transaction processing systems. With countless top big data technologies available, it can be challenging to know which ones will truly drive business value. This guide provides 10 expert insights to help you navigate the landscape of top big data platforms, from Hadoop to Spark and beyond. For professionals who want to build and manage these powerful systems, mastering them is key. Our Data Engineer Course In Pune is designed to give you the hands-on skills needed to excel in this field. Comparing the Top Big Data Technologies You Need to Know Data! Data is deemed to be the most important and valuable asset for any organization operating in the modern business world. We all accept the fact that data is large, and it is apparently infinite. Moreover, it is complex, at times structured, and sometimes unstructured. Today, in the modern world that we live in, data processing, storage, and analysis is not a simple task, and certainly not with the traditional tools at disposal. Hence, the invention of Big Data! Let us gain an insight into the latest Big Data trends. Top 10 Insights about Big Data Platforms Through this blog, we will not only attempt and explore the latest trends associated with Big Data, but also some technologies augmenting its functionalities. Latest Big Data Platforms IBM Big Data Platform IBM is considered being a comprehensive big data platform addressing all the big data challenges encountered by businesses. The core competencies of IBM Big Data Platform are information integration & governance, Hadoop-based analytics, data-warehousing, and stream computing. It is an incorporation of traditional technologies and modern-day technologies. The traditional technologies facilitate structured and repeated tasks. On the other hand, new technologies facilitate flexibility and speed and are perfect for the exploration of unstructured data analysis and ad-hoc data exploration. SAP HANA SAP HANA is looked at as a smart choice, since it focuses on running the analytics applications more smartly, thus expediting business processes and helping to create simpler data infrastructures. HANA formulated for next-generation analytics and applications. SAP HANA acts as the foundation for all the data requirements by enabling the integration of all sorts of data, and through the application of advanced analytical processing to seek detailed information. Pivotal Big Data Suite Pivotal Big Data Suite is considered to be an extremely useful database technology, as it helps organizations accelerate the process of digital transformation. It aims at enabling a comprehensive and broad base for modern data architectures. It is based on open-source technologies. Another good thing about Pivotal Big Data Suite is that it can be deployed on-premise as well as in public clouds. Hottest Big Data Technologies Data Integration Data integration comprised of tools used in data orchestration throughout solutions such as Apache Pig, Hadoop, Apache HIVE, etc. Data Virtualization Data virtualization is a technology that relays information through different big data sources like Hadoop, and through distributed data stores in real-time and near real-time. Predictive Analytics Predictive analytics could be termed as hardware and/or software solutions allowing businesses to find out, assess, maximize, and employ predictive models through the analysis of big data sources to reduce risk and augment business performance. Data Quality Data quality is comprised of data cleansing and data enhancement products, delivering these essentials on large, high-speed datasets, through the application of parallel operations on distributed databases and data stores. Big Data Trends Big Data – Now More Approachable and Quicker Hadoop is certainly useful to perform sentiment analysis and machine learning. However, businesses are often concerned with the speed of the interactive SQL. It is because; SQL is a channel for businesses that intend to use Hadoop data for quicker exploratory analysis and recurring KPI dashboards. Big data has now become quicker and more approachable by embracing new and quicker database technologies such as MemSQL, Exasol, Hadoop-based stores like Kudu, etc. Businesses Demanding for Options Beyond Hadoop Earlier, most of the Big Data-based technologies focused on fulfilling the need for analytics on Hadoop. However, companies now are demanding multiple options beyond Hadoop. Experts believe that platforms that date and source uncertainty will tend to survive, while those built only for Hadoop and do not succeed in deploying across use cases may be ignored by businesses. Big Data Investments Yes, one cannot discount the significance of high-volume, high-variety, and high-velocity information assets. However, the most important aspect propelling investments into Big Data is the variety. Experts believe that this trend will continue to flourish, as organizations look forward to integrating additional sources and focus on the long tail of Big Data. It’s a natural next step for those who already understand DevOps basics and want to specialize in cloud-native environments specifically. Learners explore how raw data is collected, cleaned, and transformed into meaningful insights using tools like Python, R, and SQL alongside machine learning concepts. Companies across healthcare, banking, retail, and e-commerce rely heavily on data scientists to forecast trends, reduce risk, and personalize customer experiences. Average Salary: ₹7-18 LPA, given rapid AI adoption across sectors. 7. Java Course Java has powered enterprise software for decades and continues to be the backbone of banking systems, large-scale web applications, and Android development. The course covers fundamental syntax, the fundamentals of object-oriented programming, and well-known production-use frameworks like Spring and Hibernate. It’s a solid choice for learners who want a stable, well-documented language with a massive global developer community to fall back on. Even as newer languages gain attention, Java’s reliability keeps it firmly embedded in mission-critical enterprise systems worldwide. Duration: 4 to 6 months, covering core and advanced Java along with Spring and Hibernate. Career Opportunities: Java Developer, Backend Engineer, Application Developer. Because it doesn’t demand prior coding experience, Python is often the recommended starting point for complete beginners entering tech. Learners typically prepare for industry-recognized AWS certifications, which carry significant weight with hiring managers across the globe. This is still one of the most in-demand IT skill sets as more businesses switch from traditional data centers to cloud infrastructure. This course suits IT professionals who want a sense of purpose alongside technical challenge, since the work directly protects businesses and individuals from financial and reputational harm. Common applications of AI Chatbots with intelligence Systems for detecting fraud Suggestion engines Solutions for predictive analytics Real-world example: Online shopping platforms use AI-powered recommendations developed with Java technologies to suggest products based on customer preferences. 3.
